claims.nodeLabel: DoD Instruction 3204.01 - Oversight of Independent Research and Development
claims.sourceText: DoD Instruction 3204.01, 20 August 2014, incorporating Change 2, 9 July 2020
claims.text: IR&D costs 'will be allowable as indirect expenses on covered contracts to the extent they are allocable and reasonable'; reporting is required only of major contractors allocating over $11 million in IR&D and B&P costs, via project summaries reviewed for cost allowability.

claims.sourceText: Board inference from Wood's account and DoDI 3204.01 IR&D structure
claims.text: McDonnell Douglas's interest was corporate self-protection - a prime contractor conducting proprietary research into an aerospace capability it did not possess. Reasoning: this matches the incentive structure later codified in DoD IR&D policy and named by Grusch, but no McDonnell Douglas internal record of the study has been released.

claims.sourceText: DoD Instruction 3204.01, 20 August 2014, incorporating Change 2, 9 July 2020
claims.text: Corporate independent research and development is recoverable as an indirect expense on covered DoD contracts under DoD Instruction 3204.01, with project reporting required only of contractors allocating more than $11 million in IR&D and bid-and-proposal costs.

b.label: DoD Instruction 3204.01 - Oversight of Independent Research and Development

edges.label: Grusch named contractor IR&D under oath as the funding channel for concealed UAP work
edges.note: Asked whether corporations overcharge government with the excess flowing to programs, Grusch answered 'Correct, through something called IR&D,' adding that 'IR&D is literally internal to the contractors... they do whatever they want.'

a.label: DoD Instruction 3204.01 - Oversight of Independent Research and Development

b.label: FY2024 NDAA sec. 1687 - Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs

edges.label: Congress legislated directly against the IR&D mechanism, citing the instruction by number and change date
edges.note: Sec. 1687(b) makes UAP-related IR&D unallowable as an indirect expense unless disclosed to the defense and intelligence committees and congressional leadership. A statute does not cite an accounting instruction that precisely unless someone has explained how it is being used.

edges.label: Wood ran a company-funded study of unidentified craft at McDonnell Douglas Astronautics
edges.note: Wood spent his career at the Huntington Beach astronautics organisation and has repeatedly described initiating an internal study on the reasoning that a prime could not afford to be last to know if the propulsion were real.

a.label: FY2024 NDAA sec. 1687 - Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs

edges.label: The IR&D restriction applies directly to covered prime contractors
edges.note: DoDI 3204.01 covers major contractors allocating over $11 million in IR&D and bid-and-proposal costs; the primes on this board are all covered contractors, and none has publicly reported a disclosure under Sec. 1687(b).

a.label: FY2024 NDAA sec. 1687 - Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs

b.label: Waived unacknowledged special access program (waived USAP)

edges.note: The section acts on the mechanism without touching it. Sec. 1687(a) conditions obligation of funds on the Secretary reporting the activity to the defense and intelligence committees and congressional leadership; it does not repeal or amend 10 U.S.C. 119(e). The waiver stays lawful and the money stops instead.

b.label: DoD Instruction 3204.01 - Oversight of Independent Research and Development

edges.label: Corporate self-funded UAP research is the historical precedent for the IR&D channel
edges.note: Robert Wood's late-1960s company-funded study at Huntington Beach is the earliest described instance of a prime studying the phenomenon on internal money with no reporting obligation - the pattern later formalised in IR&D policy. No company record of the study has been released.
